Handbreadth of days: broad transience theme; covered by Ps 90.
yitsbor: heaps up without knowing who gathers; tsavar heap only, false friend for sabr.
God our refuge, help in tsarot (straits, root tsrr tightness): refuge for the pressed, as in ¶18.
Evening, morning and noon prayer: three stations, not the two edges of ¶4.
Three temporal stations: see the other Ps 55:18 connection.
Rain softens furrows: rain-chain covered by Isa 55:10.
Year crowned with goodness: keyword-only: good year.
Seventy or eighty years pass swiftly: general; the Ps 90 block uses 90:4-6,12.
Textual: 90:11 asks who knows the power of your anger; the seventy-years statement is 90:10.
Teach us to number our days: the given span to be counted, as with 35:37 in ¶6.
A thousand years like yesterday when past: time shrinking when seen from its end (¶6).
Swept away as a sleep, in the morning like grass: the morning half of the morning/evening life image (¶6, 79:46).
Textual: 90:7 is consumed by your anger; the morning-flourish/evening-wither line is 90:6, opened and used instead.
Fruitful in old age: keyword-only: old age.
Morning and nights praise: pair formula, but adds nothing beyond Exod 29:39 for ¶4.
Oath that they shall not enter my rest: oath-exception structure belongs to the surah or 103:3 page.
Refuge under his wings: keyword-only: refuge.
Ruth gleans among sheaves: narrative instance of the gleaning law; Deut 24:19-21 carries the point for ¶16.
Extra stalks left for Ruth: see Ruth 2:15.
Boaz as near kinsman and redeemer: keyword-only: kinship (¶17 unsur).
Kinship as refuge: keyword-only.
Winds blow on the garden so its spices flow: wind and fragrance together (¶20).
Scent lifted by wind as against storm dust: same verse (¶20).
Ask rain in the season of latter rain: keyword-only: rain clouds.
keyword-only: testing/refining like gold; no shared image with pressing, time or refuge on this page.
Corpus Coranicum (Sinai) prefers Robinson's reading of asr as end-of-market-day reckoning and leaves Neuwirth's prayer-time reading open; cited in the ¶2 minha block and the ¶5 Matt 20 block.
Editors' note: asr probably a specific time of day rather than time in general; context for the kommentar; no Jewish or Christian text is attached (no intertext entries for 103:1).
bi nishba'ti ne'um YHWH: God swears by himself; the object of the divine oath differs from 103:1 (¶1).
Since he had no one greater to swear by, he swore by himself: the Christian reading of Gen 22:16 used on ¶1.
Passover lamb slaughtered ben ha-arbayim: second attestation of the dual day-edge term (¶4).
Cornelius: I was praying at the ninth hour in my house; the ninth-hour prayer (¶2).
In the morning it flourishes, in the evening it fades and withers: the morning/evening life image (¶6); the discovery cited 90:7 in error.
Scoffers ask where the promise of his coming is: the asked-about Hour, answered by 3:8-9 (¶6).
The other virgins come later and say Lord, open to us: the late arrival (¶5).
I do not know you: the door stays shut on the late-comers (¶5).
leshonam ba-tsama nashatta: their tongue is parched with thirst, and the LORD will answer them; the dried tongue of ¶9.
The suckling's tongue cleaves for thirst: same image as Isa 41:17, which is used; no independent addition.
If the clouds are full of rain they empty it on the earth: cloud as a vessel that is emptied, beside the pressed clouds of ¶8.
He binds up waters in his clouds and the cloud is not split: cloud holding water; the holding point is made with the cognate root elsewhere; no independent addition.
Pressing (mits) milk brings butter, pressing the nose blood, pressing anger strife: pressure brings out what is within (¶10).
The cupbearer tells his dream: a vine before him (¶11).
Three branches, blossoms, clusters ripen into grapes: the dream preceding the pressing (¶11).
The three branches are three days: interpretive detail; context only, 40:13 carries the outcome.
va-ya'atsrehu melekh Ashshur va-ya'asrehu bet kele: the root used for confining a prisoner; supports ¶11's link of holding and imprisonment.
Jeremiah atsur in the court of the guard: detained/confined with the same root (¶11).
Joseph put in bet ha-sohar: Genesis names Joseph's prison with other words, not atsar (¶11).
If you detain me (ta'tsereni) I will not eat your bread: detaining sense (¶14).
Frogs heaped (va-yitsberu) in heaps: tsavar heap; confirms the false-friend judgement for sabr; no block.
Maskil of David when he was in the cave, a prayer: prayer in the cave of refuge (¶19).
Your mother was like a vine planted by waters, fruitful: the watered vine whose ruin follows (¶21).
The land of a rich man produced plentifully: opening of the stored-harvest parable (¶16).
Where shall I gather my fruits: the hoarding plan (¶16).
No one hired us; go into the vineyard: context of 20:6; no independent addition.
Prayer as incense, lifted hands as minhat arev: the evening offering bridges offering and prayer, but the ¶2 point is carried by Mishnah Berakhot 4:1 and Berakhot 26b; no independent addition.
Daniel prays three times a day toward Jerusalem: three stations, not the two edges of ¶4 or an afternoon hour (¶2).
Hebrew Ben Sira at this locator warns against a boastful tongue and slackness; it does not carry the open-to-receive/closed-to-give hand of the Greek numbering; witness/numbering mismatch.
Isaac instituted the minha (afternoon) prayer, reading Gen 24:63 lifnot erev as prayer; supports the ¶2 afternoon-prayer block.
Reads Job 28:3 as God fixing how many years Joseph would spend in prison darkness; prison measured by a span (¶11).
Two years added to Joseph for saying remember me and mention me, with a second reason (Pharaoh's dream); explains the prolonged wait of ¶12.
This Hebrew recension of Tobit 4:7 concerns Tobit's deposited silver, not the alms saying cited by the reader; textual mismatch.
Fixes the minha prayer until evening (R. Judah: until plag ha-minha); a prayer bounded by the late afternoon (¶2).
R. Tarfon: the day is short, the work much, the master presses; the late-day narrowing of ¶5.
Not your duty to finish the work: sequel to 2:15 about obligation and reward; no independent addition to ¶5.
Open shop and ledger with collectors: credit/judgment image; the page makes no ledger claim; keyword-only: reckoning.
This world as vestibule to the world to come: broad eschatological theme; keyword-only.
One hour of repentance and good deeds: concerns the good works of 103:3, not an image of this page.
Four character types (mine and yours): sharing theme; ¶14 withholding is carried more concretely by Deut 15:7-8.
Honi sleeps seventy years hidden by a rock enclosure and wakes to a generation that does not recognise him; long protected sleep (¶19).
Righteous tested like gold in a furnace: keyword-only: testing; no shared pressing, time or refuge image.
